records.title: When sex reversal keeps sex chromosomes young
records.description: In this Journal Club, Wen-Juan Ma revisits the ‘fountain-of-youth’ hypothesis proposed by Nicolas Perrin in 2009, whereby occasional sex reversal enables X–Y recombination and can thereby maintain homomorphic sex chromosomes over evolutionary time.

records.title: Genomics for chronic overlapping pain conditions
records.description: Genomic studies are revealing shared genetic susceptibility across chronic pain conditions traditionally viewed as distinct disorders. In this Comment, Wainberg et al. argue that these findings support the concept of nociplastic pain and have important implications for disease classification, clinical trials and therapeutic development.

records.title: Sequencing and analysis of the human adaptive immune receptor repertoire
records.description: This Review examines how T cell and B cell receptor repertoires are generated and shaped by genetic variation, surveys experimental and computational approaches for their analysis and highlights emerging applications, recent advances and key challenges in adaptive immune receptor repertoire research.

records.title: Tracing cell fate in space and time with SPACE-seq
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yuemeng Jia describes SPACE-seq. By combining lineage tracing with spatial transcriptomics, SPACE-seq connects lineage history to molecular state and tissue context, enabling insight into how tissue niches shape cell fate and clonal behaviour.

records.title: Decoupling cis and trans transcriptional influences
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Selin Jessa discusses a 2008 paper by Wilson et al. that used a transchromosomic mouse model to show that species-specific gene expression is determined by variation in cis sequence rather than in trans -acting factors.

records.title: Small variant calling in the era of long-read sequencing
records.description: Long-read sequencing is expanding the scope of small-variant detection, enabling analysis of genomic regions that were previously difficult to interrogate. In this Review, the authors examine approaches for long-read small-variant calling across sequencing platforms and applications, highlighting advances in deep learning, assembly-based and pangenome-based methods, benchmarking strategies and future challenges.

records.title: Towards equitable population epigenomics: implications for global health
records.description: Population epigenomic studies remain heavily skewed towards participants of European genetic ancestries, limiting the discovery and translation of DNA methylation associations across contexts. The Diverse Epigenetic Epidemiology Partnership outlines priorities for building a more equitable global epigenomics research agenda and improving the relevance of epigenetic insights for global health.

records.title: Towards a rational terminology for cell types
records.description: In this Comment, the authors outline how the lack of a consistent evolutionary framework for defining and naming cell types complicates comparisons across species and obscures questions of homology. As a solution, they propose that cell-type nomenclature be grounded in evolutionary theory by identifying conserved regulatory cores and explicitly incorporating phylogenetic origins into cell-type names.

records.title: Gene regulation at the early human maternal–fetal interface
records.description: Human placentation establishes a dynamic maternal–fetal interface in which fetal trophoblast cells coordinate tissue remodelling, immune adaptation and resource exchange to support pregnancy. In this Review, the authors discuss how single-cell, spatial and functional omics are uncovering gene regulatory mechanisms underlying trophoblast differentiation and maternal interactions and how these insights are advancing understanding of healthy placentation and pregnancy disorders.

records.title: Histone acetylation finds its link to transcription
records.description: In this Journal Club, Liling Wan highlights a 1996 paper by Brownell et al. that linked a transcriptional coactivator to histone acetyltransferase activity, which contributed to the foundation of chromatin biology today, and reflects on the lessons it offers about the enduring value of curiosity-driven research.

records.title: Mapping genetic risk to regulatory networks at single-cell resolution
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yunlong Ma describes scMORE, a framework that integrates GWAS and single-cell multi-omic data to identify trait-associated regulatory networks in specific cell types and states.

records.title: The African DSI DataBank: a federated infrastructure for Africa’s genomic and biodiversity data
records.description: The African DSI DataBank is a new federated platform designed to support African stewardship, governance and sharing of biodiversity and agricultural digital sequence information. This Comment outlines its architecture, rationale and roadmap for enabling African institutions to host, manage and contribute genomic and other biomolecular data types while retaining local control.

records.title: How cells remember sex
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Bruno Hudry discusses how Thomas Cline’s 1984 paper on the role of Sex-lethal in sex determination in Drosophila melanogaster illustrates the power of classical genetic experiments.

records.title: Is genome-wide epigenetic reprogramming a eutherian innovation?
records.description: New methylome data from marsupials indicate that genome-wide DNA methylation erasure is restricted to extraembryonic tissues. Ozren Bogdanovic discusses the implications of these findings for understanding the evolution and developmental functions of epigenetic reprogramming in mammals.

records.title: Decoding epithelial–mesenchymal transitions with multi-omics
records.description: Epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a dynamic cell-state transition that underpins embryonic development, tissue repair and ageing and is frequently co-opted in disease. In this Review, Narwade and Nieto discuss how single-cell, spatial and integrative multi-omics approaches, together with computational frameworks, are revealing EMT heterogeneity, trajectories, mechanisms and translational opportunities.

records.title: Inheritance and selection of the mitochondrial genome
records.description: Despite a high mutation rate and maternal inheritance, mitochondrial genomes remain remarkably stable across generations. This Review explores how the mitochondrial bottleneck and purifying selection shape mitochondrial DNA inheritance and examines the mechanisms that limit the transmission of deleterious variants.

records.title: Chromosomal chaos surrenders to logic
records.description: In this Journal Club, Kamila Naxerova reflects on two landmark studies by Knouse et al. and Davoli et al. that helped explain how disrupted epithelial tissue architecture promotes aneuploidy and why particular patterns of chromosome gain and loss recur across cancers.

records.title: Machine learning and statistical methods for molecular quantitative trait loci
records.description: Molecular quantitative trait loci (molQTLs) provide key insights into how non-coding variants shape complex traits and disease. In this Review, the authors outline statistical and machine learning approaches for molQTL mapping and downstream analyses, including confounder correction, fine-mapping and colocalization, as well as the integration of pleiotropy, epistasis and causal mechanisms in molQTL models.

records.title: A Middle East collaborative for undiagnosed diseases
records.description: Undiagnosed disease networks advance the discovery of genes associated with rare diseases. However, a considerable gap in discovery remains, and genomic resources continue to exhibit population bias. A collaborative initiative in the Middle East could harness unique population structure, extensive family lineages and underrepresented genomic diversity to enhance local diagnostic capabilities and facilitate global gene discovery.

records.title: The many faces of malaria parasites
records.description: In this Journal Club, Elena Gómez-Díaz highlights two studies that established the Malaria Cell Atlas, demonstrating how single-cell transcriptomics can resolve parasite heterogeneity across development, transmission and natural infections to advance malaria research.

records.title: Gene regulatory mechanisms downstream of DNA methylation
records.description: In this Review, Buckley et al. discuss how DNA methylation is interpreted in mammals and plants, focusing on the reader proteins and transcription factors that bind to methylated DNA and the downstream mechanisms by which they regulate transcriptional and epigenetic states.

records.title: The TWAS legacy: from biobanks and inaccessible tissues to virtual biology
records.description: In this Journal Club, Xiaoyu Song discusses a landmark paper by Gamazon et al. that introduced PrediXcan, which enabled the integration of tissue-specific transcriptomic information with population-scale genetic studies, laying the foundation for transcriptome-wide association studies.

records.title: The shared evolutionary capacities of plasmids and extrachromosomal DNA
records.description: Plasmids in bacteria and extrachromosomal DNA in cancer both generate copy-number variation, alter gene expression and promote rapid adaptation. In this Perspective, Shaw and Henssen explore their shared evolutionary capacities and argue that these extrachromosomal genetic elements can be viewed as convergent contingency loci with implications for evolution, drug resistance and therapeutic opportunities.

records.title: Genomic insights into natural selection in recent human history
records.description: Advances in genome-wide selection scans and ancient DNA have greatly expanded our ability to study human evolution. This Review discusses the conceptual and statistical challenges in identifying and interpreting selection signals, and how recent approaches are reshaping our understanding of human evolution over the past 10,000 years.

records.title: Zebrafish relatives as models for functional comparative genetics and genomics
records.description: Comparative functional genetics and genomics across Danio , Devario and Danionella species reveal molecular and cellular bases of phenotypic divergence, establishing danionin fishes as powerful model systems for understanding a wide range of evolutionary innovations.

records.title: The mechanistic and evolutionary diversity of programmed DNA elimination
records.description: Programmed DNA elimination is a developmentally regulated process in which specific DNA sequences are reproducibly removed from particular cell lineages. Here, the authors review the mechanistic diversity and evolutionary dynamics of DNA elimination, spanning chromosome breakage, whole-chromosome elimination and whole-genome elimination.

records.title: Programmable enzymes for targeted gene insertion
records.description: The programmable insertion of large DNA sequences could overcome fundamental limitations of current genome-editing technologies. In this Review, Lampe, King and Sternberg describe recent advances in recombinases, retrotransposons and CRISPR-associated transposases, and discuss how these systems are enabling mutation-agnostic genome modification.

records.title: Species-dense genomics through natural history collections
records.description: Large-scale genome initiatives are transforming biodiversity genomics, but genomes remain taxonomically sparse and difficult to compare across species. Kapli and colleagues argue that natural history collections should play a central role in building species-dense genomic resources, creating the foundation needed for comparative and predictive biodiversity genomics.

records.title: How telomere attrition protects against cancer
records.description: In this Review, the authors discuss recent data showing that telomere attrition is a powerful tumour-suppressor mechanism that limits the development of a wide variety of human cancers.

records.title: Bridging precision agriculture and human medicine through comparative genetics
records.description: In this Review, Liu et al. describe advances that are enabling comparative genetic studies of humans and farmed animals, which have the potential to generate insights that are beneficial for both biomedical research and agriculture.

records.title: Endogenous retroviruses in development and cell fate specification
records.description: In this Journal Club, Hongqing Liang reflects on a landmark study by Macfarlan et al. that linked endogenous retrovirus activity to totipotent-like cell states, reshaping our understanding of developmental plasticity and cell fate specification.

records.title: Proteogenomics in human populations
records.description: Proteogenomics integrates genomic and proteomic data to reveal how genetic variation influences protein abundance and contributes to human disease. In this Review, the authors focus on protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL), highlighting advances in pQTL mapping, biological interpretation and emerging applications.

records.title: A transcription factor hustles towards a precise target
records.description: In this Journal Club, Wulan Deng highlights a landmark paper by Elf et al. that used single-molecule imaging in living bacteria to reveal how transcription factors locate specific DNA targets through a dynamic, largely stochastic search process.

records.title: Gene expression evolution at the dawn of RNA-seq
records.description: In this Journal Club, Camille Berthelot highlights a 2011 paper by Brawand et al. that used early RNA-sequencing data across several mammalian species to determine how gene expression evolves, identifying tissue-specific rates of change and signatures of adaptation.

records.title: Using genetics to mimic drug interactions
records.description: In this Journal Club, Pamela Yeh recalls a landmark study by Bollenbach et al. that used genetic perturbations in Escherichia coli to uncover the mechanism underlying a classic suppressive drug interaction.

records.title: Genetics and genomics of hybridization
records.description: Hybridization, the exchange of genes between divergent lineages, is now recognized as widespread across eukaryotes and essential to understanding genome evolution. In this Review, Schumer and Rieseberg overview methodological advances facilitating recent progress, reassess the frequency, causes and consequences of hybridization, and highlight key open questions.

records.title: AI-based multimodal integration of genomics and electronic health records
records.description: This Review covers advances in artificial intelligence-based methods for multimodal modelling of genomics and electronic health record data, and the integration of these data into electronic-health-record-based research and clinical workflows to support genomics-enabled clinical decision, with an emphasis on governance and equitable implementation.

records.title: The genetics of complex gene expression phenotypes illuminated
records.description: Christian Landry reflects on a 2002 study by Brem, Yvert and colleagues, which combined yeast genetics and genome-wide expression profiling to reveal the genetic architecture underlying gene expression and transformed our understanding of regulatory variation.

records.title: Embracing non-linearity in human ageing
records.description: Ageing has often been conceptualized as a gradual, linear decline, yet growing evidence suggests it unfolds through dynamic, stage-specific transitions. In this Perspective, the authors examine such evidence across molecular and physiological systems and discuss analytical frameworks to identify non-linear transitions.

records.title: Towards quantifying immune diversity through HLA genomics
records.description: Computational metrics such as HLA evolutionary divergence offer new ways to quantify functional variation in antigen presentation. In this Comment, the authors discuss how population-scale genomics can benchmark these approaches and assess their potential as quantitative measures of human immune diversity.

records.title: Genomic, epigenomic and transcriptomic regulation of cellular senescence
records.description: Senescence — a complex, dynamic and heterogeneous stress-responsive cell state — shapes ageing biology and tissue homeostasis. This Review examines the molecular regulation of senescence initiation, maintenance and propagation, highlighting the need for revised mechanistic frameworks and biomarkers to define and target senescent cells.

records.title: Human genetics across levels of biological organization
records.description: Genetic variation influences biological processes across scales; however, deciphering how effects propagate from molecules to whole organisms remains a key challenge in human genetics. In this Review, Laman Trip and Beltrao discuss how to link genetic variation to mechanisms across interacting biological levels using network, single-cell and imaging approaches.

records.title: Stomata — guarding the gates against bacterial invasion
records.description: In this Journal Club, Tatsuya Nobori recalls a landmark paper by Melotto et al., who showed that stomata are active components of plant innate immunity rather than passive entry points for bacterial pathogens.

records.title: Folding a broken genome: the versatile roles of cohesin in genome maintenance
records.description: The protein complex cohesin shapes 3D genome organization through both cohesion and loop extrusion. The authors review the roles of these two mechanistic functions in the cellular response to DNA double-strand breaks, wherein cohesin acts to signal the presence of DNA damage, establish a repair environment, and catalyse the DNA repair process.

records.title: Genetic analysis of imaging-derived phenotypes
records.description: When integrated with genetic data, imaging-derived phenotypes (IDPs) enable large-scale analyses of genotype–phenotype relationships. Bian and Akey review analytical approaches to derive IDPs, key biological insights from genetic studies of imaging traits and emerging challenges in the rapidly evolving field of imaging genomics.

records.title: Building and applying pangenome references to capture genetic diversity
records.description: Pangenomes are genome references that integrate sequences from multiple individuals into graph-based or multi-haplotype representations, capturing genetic variation beyond a single linear reference. Here the authors review advances in assembling and applying human pangenome references, highlighting tools, insights and remaining challenges.

records.title: Genetic origins and constraints of evolutionary innovation
records.description: Evolutionary innovation emerges through the interplay of genetic novelty, genomic architecture and evolutionary constraint. Nature Reviews Genetics presents a Focus issue that explores the mechanisms that generate, integrate and shape biological diversity.

records.title: Single-cell four-omics with CHARM
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yujie Chen describes CHARM, a single-cell four-omics sequencing method that profiles genome conformation, chromatin accessibility, histone modifications and gene expression.

records.title: Molecular integration of seasonal temperature signals in flowering time control
records.description: Plants must accurately time flowering by integrating seasonal temperature cues to ensure reproductive success. This Review describes how two mechanisms — rapid transcriptional responses and long-term epigenetic memory — work together in parallel to robustly control flowering time, and it highlights that variation in these processes provides important information for the future of crops under a changing climate.

records.title: RBPscan measures protein–RNA interactions in living cells
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Dmitry Kretov and Daniel Cifuentes describe RBPscan (RNA-binding protein specificity and contextual analysis via nucleotide editing), a method that measures the strength of in vivo interactions between RNA binding proteins and their RNA targets.

records.title: Revisiting retinal and macular degeneration in the genomics era
records.description: Retinal and macular degeneration are major causes of vision loss around the globe. In this Review, Swaroop and Roska outline the genetic underpinnings of these eye diseases increasingly revealed by technological advances, while also highlighting mechanistic patterns that can inform therapeutic intervention to restore vision.

records.title: How evolution builds three morphs from one genome
records.description: Sarah Kocher reflects on two influential 2016 studies in the ruff that demonstrated how a large genomic inversion links variation across multiple traits into a single ‘supergene’.

records.title: Advancing the applications of liquid biopsies in oncology
records.description: In this Review, Valpione et al. discuss how the current applications of liquid biopsies in precision oncology might be expanded to provide a more holistic and personalized view of cancer and to improve cancer diagnosis and treatment.

records.title: Pleiotropic effects of cis -regulatory mutations
records.description: In this Comment, Patricia Wittkopp revisits assumptions that cis -regulatory mutations are weakly pleiotropic, ultimately calling for more data to assess the extent to which they are less pleiotropic and deleterious than trans -regulatory mutations.

records.title: Transposable elements as catalysts of evolutionary innovation
records.description: In this Comment, Cedric Feschotte highlights evidence from diverse lineages showing that transposable elements are key drivers of evolutionary innovation, repeatedly introducing regulatory and coding sequences that reconfigure genome function.

records.title: Adaptation: by giant leaps or many tiny steps?
records.description: In this Comment, the authors argue that understanding the genetic basis of adaptation requires considering the genetic architecture and ecological properties of traits under selection. They propose a framework that predicts when evolution proceeds by many small changes or few large-effect variants, and when its genetic basis should be predictable across populations and species.

records.title: Written in blood: DNA methylation in liquid biopsy
records.description: In this Journal Club, Chatterjee and Rodger highlight two studies by Guo et al. and Shen et al. that demonstrated how genome-wide DNA methylation profiling enables sensitive detection and classification of tumour-derived cell-free DNA, advancing epigenetic approaches in liquid biopsy for cancer diagnostics.

records.title: Single-cell trimodal profiling with scHiCAR
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yueyuan Xu and Xiaolin Wei discuss scHiCAR (single-cell Hi-C with assay for transposase-accessible chromatin and RNA sequencing), a trimodal single-cell method for simultaneously profiling gene expression, chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organization.

records.title: Translating functional molecular knowledge into crop-breeding success
records.description: In this Perspective, Ramstein and colleagues discuss the use of emerging machine learning tools for function-informed prioritization of variants for plant breeding; they outline future applications in which precision breeding strategies have the potential to be most effective.

records.title: The discovery of gene imprinting
records.description: In this Journal Club, Mary Gehring recalls a 1970 paper from Jerry Kermicle, which used elegant maize genetics to show that alleles behave differently depending on parental origin, laying the conceptual foundation for gene imprinting.

records.title: The long reach of the Red Queen
records.description: Red Queen dynamics describe a mode of evolution in which interacting biological entities continually adapt and counteradapt. This Comment discusses the pervasiveness of these dynamics within genomes, which can involve selfish genetic elements, and highlights building evidence that they can even drive compensatory coevolution among subunits of essential protein complexes.

records.title: Computational approaches for multimodal lineage tracing
records.description: Multimodal lineage tracing links heritable ancestry with single-cell molecular states to reveal how cell fates emerge during development, regeneration and disease. In this Review, the authors survey key computational challenges and methods for phylogenetic inference, fate mapping and gene programme discovery.

records.title: Time matters: circadian genetics and the molecular logic of human health and disease
records.description: The circadian clock controls transcriptional and signalling networks across tissues to maintain homeostasis, with pathological consequences to its disruption. Kuo et al. review our understanding of circadian genetic and molecular mechanisms in health and disease, as well as emerging opportunities to probe and therapeutically target circadian regulation.

records.title: Immune-evasive DNA integration with INSTALL
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Connor Tou presents INSTALL, a recombinase-driven, kilobase-scale DNA integration method that employs partially duplexed circular single-stranded DNA to evade the cellular immune system.

records.title: The unbearable presence of senescent cells in ageing
records.description: Chanhee Kang highlights two papers by Baker et al. and Acosta et al. that established a role for senescent cells in age-related pathologies and revealed how the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) can influence neighbouring cells.

records.title: Resolving structural variants in pangenome graphs with Swave
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Songbo Wang introduces Swave, an AI-enhanced sequence-to-image method capable of detecting complex SVs from pangenome graphs.

records.title: Evolutionary genetics of ageing
records.description: Modern humans increasingly live long enough to experience late-life consequences of genetic and molecular systems shaped by natural selection. In this Review, the authors integrate evolutionary genetics and genetic evidence to explain why ageing evolves, why longevity varies across species and individuals, and how these insights inform healthspan extension.

records.title: RNA design across eras: from covariance models to modern generative AI
records.description: In this Journal Club, Annalisa Marsico describes a 1994 paper by Eddy and Durbin that formalized RNA sequence analysis with covariance models, which are powerful tools more recently applied to generative machine learning models for RNA design.

records.title: Prime editing: redefining precision genome editing
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Qiupeng Lin recalls the 2019 paper by Anzalone et al. that introduced prime editing, and reflects on the impact of this technology on genome biology and beyond.

records.title: Nutrition signals the brain to reactivate quiescent neural stem cells
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Hongyan Wang highlights two papers that elucidated the signalling mechanisms and inter-organ communication involved in neural stem cell reactivation in Drosophila melanogaster .

records.title: Mechanisms of DNA specificity in chromatin remodelling
records.description: In this Journal Club, Lu Bai highlights a 2021 paper by Donovan et al. that brought mechanistic clarity to the question of how chromatin remodellers achieve DNA specificity, which had been difficult to address beyond correlated localization patterns between chromatin remodellers and transcription factors.

records.title: The epigenetic nature of X chromosome inactivation
records.description: In this Journal Club, Claudia Keller Valsecchi recalls two seminal studies by Csankovszki et al. and by Wutz and Jaenisch that defined X-chromosome inactivation as an epigenetic process by revealing when Xist is required and when silencing becomes Xist -independent.

records.title: When the genome learned its own vocabulary
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Maria Brbić discusses DeepSEA, a pioneering deep convolutional neural network to predict functional effects of non-coding variants, and its influence on computational genomics.

records.title: Reading cell division histories from the methylome
records.description: In this Journal Club, Shou-Wen Wang recalls a seminal paper by Yatabe et al., which harnessed stochastic DNA methylation patterns in the human colon for epigenetic lineage tracing, and influenced the development of the computational framework MethylTree two decades later.

records.title: TimeVault: a synthetic time capsule for transcriptome storage
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yu-Kai Chao describes TimeVault, an inducible system that can store transcriptomes at defined time points, enabling temporal changes in transcriptional state to be linked to biological events.

records.title: More than meets the eye(spot): evolution through co-option of developmental programmes
records.description: In this Journal Club, Francisca Real recalls a 1999 paper by Keys et al. that dissected the mechanistic underpinnings of butterfly wing spot development, which ultimately provided one of the earliest and clearest examples of phenotypic evolution by genetic co-option.

records.title: Tools and tactics for studying alternative splicing
records.description: In this Review, Sousa-Luís and Carmo-Fonseca discuss the various tools available to detect and quantify alternative splicing, functionally test splice isoforms and investigate the link between genetic variation, splicing and disease.

records.title: CRISPR–Cas-based live cell imaging of genome dynamics
records.description: In this Review, Zhu et al. outline the various CRISPR-based tools recently built for dynamic DNA and RNA imaging, which have provided insights into various molecular mechanisms. The authors also discuss the important parameters to consider when using these tools, and how to approach the quantitative image analysis.

records.title: DNA assembly with Sidewinder via 3-way junctions
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Kaihang Wang describes Sidewinder, a new tool that leverages ‘page number’ barcodes and 3-way junctions to scarlessly assemble DNA with high fidelity, expanding the scope of what DNA writing can achieve.

records.title: Unlocking the potential of pedigree genomics via precision governance
records.description: China’s large, multi-generational pedigrees provide a distinctive genomic resource for precision medicine but present a governance challenge. We propose a new framework that addresses the core contradiction between individual-centric governance and the collective nature of these genomic datasets.

records.title: Unlocking the potential of pedigree genomics via precision governance
records.description: China’s large, multi-generational pedigrees provide a distinctive genomic resource for precision medicine but present a governance challenge. We propose a new framework that addresses the core contradiction between individual-centric governance and the collective nature of these genomic datasets.

records.title: How classical genetics uncovered key determinants of TE silencing
records.description: In this Journal Club, Emilie Brasset highlights a 1995 publication by Prud’homme et al., who designed a clever genetic assay to identify a gene important for TE silencing, which provided a crucial foundation for later studies to unravel the underlying mechanisms.

records.title: Genetic influences on haematopoiesis
records.description: Haematopoiesis is a classic process for understanding the genetic basis of human health and disease. In this Review, Poeschla and Sankaran discuss this history and more recent advances in our understanding of the roles of rare variants in monogenic blood diseases, germline and somatic variants in population-level variation, as well as emerging therapeutic applications.

records.title: Author Correction: Forensic genetics in the omics era
Recoding genomes with programmed ribosomal frameshifting
records.description: In this Journal Club, Yousuf A. Khan recounts a landmark study published in 1985 by Jacks and Varmus that documented programmed ribosomal frameshifting in retroviruses, which later inspired Yousuf to search for this phenomenon in vertebrates.

records.title: Next-generation programmable cell therapies for precision medicine
records.description: In this Review, Teixeira et al. discuss emerging strategies for developing and improving engineered-cell therapies. They outline progress from ex vivo engineered autologous cells to in vivo reprogramming, advances in delivery systems and the remaining translational barriers.

records.title: Gene regulatory networks: from correlative models to causal explanations
records.description: In this Perspective, Maizels and Briscoe discuss the limitations of current models of gene regulatory networks and outline solutions to harness data abundance without compromising explanatory power.

records.title: Epistasis and co-adaptation in bacterial genome evolution
records.description: Bacterial genome evolution is shaped by epistasis, which can constrain or promote specific evolutionary paths. The authors review how integrating the effects of epistatic interactions into population-scale analyses can improve genotype–phenotype mapping and provide a deeper understanding of the complex traits that shape the microbial world.

records.title: Charting single-cell lineages with synthetic and natural barcodes
records.description: In this Review, Rodriguez-Fraticelli and Parreno discuss advances in single-cell lineage-tracing methods and how their application to diverse biological processes, such as development, ageing and cancer, is challenging prevailing views and providing new insights.

records.title: From DNA microarrays to somatic mosaicism in population cohorts
records.description: Chikashi Terao recalls a paper by Loh et al., which introduced a highly sensitive algorithm to detect low-fraction chromosomal mosaicism from SNP array data, enabling large-scale mapping of clonal haematopoiesis.

records.title: A codon-resolved view of subcellular translation with LOCL-TL
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Jingchuan Luo discusses LOCL-TL (LOV domain-controlled ligase for translation localization), a method they helped develop to enable the study of subcellular translation at codon-level resolution.

records.title: Annotating genomes at increased scale and resolution
records.description: In this Review, Ji et al. overview how rapidly advancing experimental and computational methods are enabling improved and automated annotation of gene structure and function, providing researchers with genome annotation resources of unprecedented scale and resolution.

records.title: Bridging technical innovation and computational advances in studies of RNA–protein assemblies
records.description: Empirical and artificial intelligence-based approaches are redefining how RNA-dependent protein assemblies are mapped, modelled and targeted, revealing their dynamic roles in health and disease and outlining closed-loop strategies for predictive functional RNA and ribonucleoprotein design.

records.title: Evolutionary causes and consequences of gene duplication
records.description: Gene duplication is a key evolutionary mechanism, as initially redundant paralogues diverge over time. The authors review how adaptive and non-adaptive forces influence the evolutionary fates of gene duplicates, highlighting the importance of function–fitness relationships and gene expression dynamics.

records.title: Massively parallel reporter assays: from barcodes to biology
records.description: In this Journal Club, Fumitaka Inoue discusses a 2009 paper by Patwardhan et al. that introduced a massively parallel saturation-mutagenesis assay that leverages high-throughput DNA synthesis and sequencing to quantify the effects of single-nucleotide changes on regulatory element activity.

records.title: Revisiting the blueprint for an interpretable virtual cell
records.description: In this Journal Club, Angela Ruohao Wu highlights a 2012 paper by Karr et al. that exemplifies the value of 'rule-based' mechanistic models in biology, prompting questions about the future of predictive biological modelling in the current era of artificial intelligence.

records.title: Revisiting the molecular workhorse: plasmids in evolutionary conflict
records.description: Campbell and Goyal discuss a recent study by Rossine et al., which introduces a synthetic plasmid system that experimentally separates within-cell from between-cell selection, revealing multilevel evolutionary conflict and addressing questions first posed by Szathmáry and Smith in 1995.

records.title: Navigating ethical, legal and social implications in genomic newborn screening
records.description: The successful implementation of genomic newborn screening involves a wide array of ethical, legal and social implications of great complexity. The authors outline key decision points and highlight a GA4GH policy tool to support responsible, trustworthy implementation within diverse public health systems globally.

records.title: The genetic foundations of convergent traits
records.description: Convergent phenotypic evolution, the independent acquisition of similar or nearly identical traits in multiple species, is widespread. Allard and Kumar explore the spectrum of molecular convergence in multicellular organisms, evaluate computational and artificial intelligence-based methods for detecting adaptive genetic convergence, and highlight how comparative genomics of convergent phenotypes informs complex trait evolution and human health.

records.title: Bridging behaviour and genomics for tsetse fly control
records.description: In this Journal Club, Daniel Masiga recalls a 1986 publication by C. H. Green, which revealed how colour and odour cues influence tsetse fly ( Glossina spp.) attraction, and a 2019 study by Attardo et al. on genomic insights across six Glossina species, advancing understanding of vector behaviour and control.

records.title: High-throughput identification of aptamer–target pairs with SPARK-seq
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Qin Wu discusses the development of SPARK-seq (single-cell perturbation-driven aptamer recognition and kinetics sequencing), a method that enables high-throughput identification of aptamer–target pairs.

records.title: Emergence and evolution of protein-coding de novo genes
records.description: De novo gene evolution entails the birth of new genes from previously non-coding DNA. In this Review, Bornberg-Bauer and Eicholt overview how protein-coding de novo genes are identified, the mechanistic and evolutionary processes underlying their emergence and evolution, and the patterns in their encoded protein structures.

records.title: Long non-coding RNAs as orchestrators of dosage compensation
records.description: In this Journal Club, Hodkinson and Larschan recall a 2002 paper by Meller and Rattner that used the power of Drosophila genetics to demonstrate the integral role of long non-coding RNAs in dosage compensation.

records.title: Bringing methylation profile scores to early life
records.description: Population epigenetics leverages methylation profile scores (MPSs) to aggregate information across multiple DNA methylation sites. In this Comment, the authors advocate for MPSs to be trained in early-life contexts, anchored in longitudinal developmental data and evaluated using harmonized standards.

records.title: Regulation of gene expression by alternative polyadenylation in health and disease
records.description: Alternative 3′-end processing of nascent RNA, known as alternative polyadenylation (APA), increases transcript diversity and augments post-transcriptional modulation of gene expression. APA profiles are highly dynamic in response to cell growth, differentiation and extracellular cues, and dysregulated APA is a hallmark of human diseases.

records.title: Monitoring biological effects of somatic cell genome editing
records.description: CRISPR-based genome editing therapeutics are entering the clinic, but in vitro and in vivo tools are needed to assess their safety and efficacy. The authors review complementary technologies to monitor the biological effects of genome editing across scales, including the direct measurement of editing outcomes in DNA, human microphysiological systems and non-invasive in vivo imaging.

records.title: Whole-genome spatial transcriptomic imaging with RAEFISH
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yubao Cheng discusses the development of RAEFISH (reverse-padlock amplicon-encoding fluorescence in situ hybridization), a method that enables spatial transcriptomics with both single-molecule spatial resolution and genome-wide coverage.

records.title: A genomic and epigenomic view of human centromeres
records.description: The complex and repetitive nature of centromeres has historically posed challenges to their genomic assembly and functional understanding, which are now being overcome with long-read sequencing. This Review discusses recent genomic and epigenomic insights into human centromere biology that have positioned the field for future studies of centromere structure in chromosome biology and human disease.

records.title: Ancestral diversity in complex disease genetics: from discovery to translation
records.description: Ancestral and geographic diversity in genomic resources can improve our understanding of complex disease genetics. The authors review how ancestrally diverse biobanks worldwide are reshaping genetic discovery, empowering the identification of novel variants and disease associations, with important biological implications.

records.title: Mapping the disease interactome
records.description: In this Journal Club, Valborg Gudmundsdottir recalls a study by Menche et al., who used a network-based approach to systematically identify clusters of connections between disease-related proteins and elucidate the molecular underpinnings of disease–disease relationships.

records.title: From models to molecules: self-organized and instructed modes of developmental patterning
records.description: In this Journal Club article, David Brückner discusses how seminal molecular genetic studies by Driever and Nüsslein-Volhard and Sick et al. demonstrated that both instructed (Wolpert model) and self-organized (Turing model) patterning occurs during animal development.

records.title: Proteoform medicine: characterizing and targeting protein forms in human disease
records.description: Proteoforms are the diverse protein molecules produced from a single gene whose primary sequence and composition can be diversified by genetic, transcriptomic, translational and post-translational variation. This Review synthesizes technologies and network approaches to map, quantify and functionally characterize proteoforms, outlining routes to proteoform-guided biomarkers and therapeutics

records.title: Let the data speak — single-cell analysis with CellWhisperer
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Moritz Schaefer introduces CellWhisperer, a multimodal machine learning model and software tool for the chat-based interrogation of single-cell RNA sequencing datasets.

records.title: Interpretation, extrapolation and perturbation of single cells
records.description: Causal and mechanistic modelling strategies, which aim to infer cause–effect relationships, provide insights into cellular responses to perturbations. The authors review computational approaches that harness machine learning and single-cell data to advance our understanding of cellular heterogeneity and causal mechanisms in biological systems.

records.title: When sex reversal keeps sex chromosomes young
records.description: In this Journal Club, Wen-Juan Ma revisits the ‘fountain-of-youth’ hypothesis proposed by Nicolas Perrin in 2009, whereby occasional sex reversal enables X–Y recombination and can thereby maintain homomorphic sex chromosomes over evolutionary time.

records.title: Genomics for chronic overlapping pain conditions
records.description: Genomic studies are revealing shared genetic susceptibility across chronic pain conditions traditionally viewed as distinct disorders. In this Comment, Wainberg et al. argue that these findings support the concept of nociplastic pain and have important implications for disease classification, clinical trials and therapeutic development.

records.title: Sequencing and analysis of the human adaptive immune receptor repertoire
records.description: This Review examines how T cell and B cell receptor repertoires are generated and shaped by genetic variation, surveys experimental and computational approaches for their analysis and highlights emerging applications, recent advances and key challenges in adaptive immune receptor repertoire research.

records.title: Tracing cell fate in space and time with SPACE-seq
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yuemeng Jia describes SPACE-seq. By combining lineage tracing with spatial transcriptomics, SPACE-seq connects lineage history to molecular state and tissue context, enabling insight into how tissue niches shape cell fate and clonal behaviour.

records.title: Decoupling cis and trans transcriptional influences
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Selin Jessa discusses a 2008 paper by Wilson et al. that used a transchromosomic mouse model to show that species-specific gene expression is determined by variation in cis sequence rather than in trans -acting factors.

records.title: Small variant calling in the era of long-read sequencing
records.description: Long-read sequencing is expanding the scope of small-variant detection, enabling analysis of genomic regions that were previously difficult to interrogate. In this Review, the authors examine approaches for long-read small-variant calling across sequencing platforms and applications, highlighting advances in deep learning, assembly-based and pangenome-based methods, benchmarking strategies and future challenges.

records.title: Towards equitable population epigenomics: implications for global health
records.description: Population epigenomic studies remain heavily skewed towards participants of European genetic ancestries, limiting the discovery and translation of DNA methylation associations across contexts. The Diverse Epigenetic Epidemiology Partnership outlines priorities for building a more equitable global epigenomics research agenda and improving the relevance of epigenetic insights for global health.

records.title: Towards a rational terminology for cell types
records.description: In this Comment, the authors outline how the lack of a consistent evolutionary framework for defining and naming cell types complicates comparisons across species and obscures questions of homology. As a solution, they propose that cell-type nomenclature be grounded in evolutionary theory by identifying conserved regulatory cores and explicitly incorporating phylogenetic origins into cell-type names.

records.title: Gene regulation at the early human maternal–fetal interface
records.description: Human placentation establishes a dynamic maternal–fetal interface in which fetal trophoblast cells coordinate tissue remodelling, immune adaptation and resource exchange to support pregnancy. In this Review, the authors discuss how single-cell, spatial and functional omics are uncovering gene regulatory mechanisms underlying trophoblast differentiation and maternal interactions and how these insights are advancing understanding of healthy placentation and pregnancy disorders.

records.title: Histone acetylation finds its link to transcription
records.description: In this Journal Club, Liling Wan highlights a 1996 paper by Brownell et al. that linked a transcriptional coactivator to histone acetyltransferase activity, which contributed to the foundation of chromatin biology today, and reflects on the lessons it offers about the enduring value of curiosity-driven research.

records.title: Mapping genetic risk to regulatory networks at single-cell resolution
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yunlong Ma describes scMORE, a framework that integrates GWAS and single-cell multi-omic data to identify trait-associated regulatory networks in specific cell types and states.

records.title: The African DSI DataBank: a federated infrastructure for Africa’s genomic and biodiversity data
records.description: The African DSI DataBank is a new federated platform designed to support African stewardship, governance and sharing of biodiversity and agricultural digital sequence information. This Comment outlines its architecture, rationale and roadmap for enabling African institutions to host, manage and contribute genomic and other biomolecular data types while retaining local control.

records.title: How cells remember sex
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Bruno Hudry discusses how Thomas Cline’s 1984 paper on the role of Sex-lethal in sex determination in Drosophila melanogaster illustrates the power of classical genetic experiments.

records.title: Is genome-wide epigenetic reprogramming a eutherian innovation?
records.description: New methylome data from marsupials indicate that genome-wide DNA methylation erasure is restricted to extraembryonic tissues. Ozren Bogdanovic discusses the implications of these findings for understanding the evolution and developmental functions of epigenetic reprogramming in mammals.

records.title: Decoding epithelial–mesenchymal transitions with multi-omics
records.description: Epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a dynamic cell-state transition that underpins embryonic development, tissue repair and ageing and is frequently co-opted in disease. In this Review, Narwade and Nieto discuss how single-cell, spatial and integrative multi-omics approaches, together with computational frameworks, are revealing EMT heterogeneity, trajectories, mechanisms and translational opportunities.

records.title: Inheritance and selection of the mitochondrial genome
records.description: Despite a high mutation rate and maternal inheritance, mitochondrial genomes remain remarkably stable across generations. This Review explores how the mitochondrial bottleneck and purifying selection shape mitochondrial DNA inheritance and examines the mechanisms that limit the transmission of deleterious variants.

records.title: Chromosomal chaos surrenders to logic
records.description: In this Journal Club, Kamila Naxerova reflects on two landmark studies by Knouse et al. and Davoli et al. that helped explain how disrupted epithelial tissue architecture promotes aneuploidy and why particular patterns of chromosome gain and loss recur across cancers.

records.title: Machine learning and statistical methods for molecular quantitative trait loci
records.description: Molecular quantitative trait loci (molQTLs) provide key insights into how non-coding variants shape complex traits and disease. In this Review, the authors outline statistical and machine learning approaches for molQTL mapping and downstream analyses, including confounder correction, fine-mapping and colocalization, as well as the integration of pleiotropy, epistasis and causal mechanisms in molQTL models.

records.title: A Middle East collaborative for undiagnosed diseases
records.description: Undiagnosed disease networks advance the discovery of genes associated with rare diseases. However, a considerable gap in discovery remains, and genomic resources continue to exhibit population bias. A collaborative initiative in the Middle East could harness unique population structure, extensive family lineages and underrepresented genomic diversity to enhance local diagnostic capabilities and facilitate global gene discovery.

records.title: The many faces of malaria parasites
records.description: In this Journal Club, Elena Gómez-Díaz highlights two studies that established the Malaria Cell Atlas, demonstrating how single-cell transcriptomics can resolve parasite heterogeneity across development, transmission and natural infections to advance malaria research.

records.title: Gene regulatory mechanisms downstream of DNA methylation
records.description: In this Review, Buckley et al. discuss how DNA methylation is interpreted in mammals and plants, focusing on the reader proteins and transcription factors that bind to methylated DNA and the downstream mechanisms by which they regulate transcriptional and epigenetic states.

records.title: The TWAS legacy: from biobanks and inaccessible tissues to virtual biology
records.description: In this Journal Club, Xiaoyu Song discusses a landmark paper by Gamazon et al. that introduced PrediXcan, which enabled the integration of tissue-specific transcriptomic information with population-scale genetic studies, laying the foundation for transcriptome-wide association studies.

records.title: The shared evolutionary capacities of plasmids and extrachromosomal DNA
records.description: Plasmids in bacteria and extrachromosomal DNA in cancer both generate copy-number variation, alter gene expression and promote rapid adaptation. In this Perspective, Shaw and Henssen explore their shared evolutionary capacities and argue that these extrachromosomal genetic elements can be viewed as convergent contingency loci with implications for evolution, drug resistance and therapeutic opportunities.

records.title: Genomic insights into natural selection in recent human history
records.description: Advances in genome-wide selection scans and ancient DNA have greatly expanded our ability to study human evolution. This Review discusses the conceptual and statistical challenges in identifying and interpreting selection signals, and how recent approaches are reshaping our understanding of human evolution over the past 10,000 years.

records.title: Zebrafish relatives as models for functional comparative genetics and genomics
records.description: Comparative functional genetics and genomics across Danio , Devario and Danionella species reveal molecular and cellular bases of phenotypic divergence, establishing danionin fishes as powerful model systems for understanding a wide range of evolutionary innovations.

records.title: The mechanistic and evolutionary diversity of programmed DNA elimination
records.description: Programmed DNA elimination is a developmentally regulated process in which specific DNA sequences are reproducibly removed from particular cell lineages. Here, the authors review the mechanistic diversity and evolutionary dynamics of DNA elimination, spanning chromosome breakage, whole-chromosome elimination and whole-genome elimination.

records.title: Programmable enzymes for targeted gene insertion
records.description: The programmable insertion of large DNA sequences could overcome fundamental limitations of current genome-editing technologies. In this Review, Lampe, King and Sternberg describe recent advances in recombinases, retrotransposons and CRISPR-associated transposases, and discuss how these systems are enabling mutation-agnostic genome modification.

records.title: Species-dense genomics through natural history collections
records.description: Large-scale genome initiatives are transforming biodiversity genomics, but genomes remain taxonomically sparse and difficult to compare across species. Kapli and colleagues argue that natural history collections should play a central role in building species-dense genomic resources, creating the foundation needed for comparative and predictive biodiversity genomics.

records.title: How telomere attrition protects against cancer
records.description: In this Review, the authors discuss recent data showing that telomere attrition is a powerful tumour-suppressor mechanism that limits the development of a wide variety of human cancers.

records.title: Bridging precision agriculture and human medicine through comparative genetics
records.description: In this Review, Liu et al. describe advances that are enabling comparative genetic studies of humans and farmed animals, which have the potential to generate insights that are beneficial for both biomedical research and agriculture.

records.title: Endogenous retroviruses in development and cell fate specification
records.description: In this Journal Club, Hongqing Liang reflects on a landmark study by Macfarlan et al. that linked endogenous retrovirus activity to totipotent-like cell states, reshaping our understanding of developmental plasticity and cell fate specification.

records.title: Proteogenomics in human populations
records.description: Proteogenomics integrates genomic and proteomic data to reveal how genetic variation influences protein abundance and contributes to human disease. In this Review, the authors focus on protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL), highlighting advances in pQTL mapping, biological interpretation and emerging applications.

records.title: A transcription factor hustles towards a precise target
records.description: In this Journal Club, Wulan Deng highlights a landmark paper by Elf et al. that used single-molecule imaging in living bacteria to reveal how transcription factors locate specific DNA targets through a dynamic, largely stochastic search process.

records.title: Gene expression evolution at the dawn of RNA-seq
records.description: In this Journal Club, Camille Berthelot highlights a 2011 paper by Brawand et al. that used early RNA-sequencing data across several mammalian species to determine how gene expression evolves, identifying tissue-specific rates of change and signatures of adaptation.

records.title: Using genetics to mimic drug interactions
records.description: In this Journal Club, Pamela Yeh recalls a landmark study by Bollenbach et al. that used genetic perturbations in Escherichia coli to uncover the mechanism underlying a classic suppressive drug interaction.

records.title: Genetics and genomics of hybridization
records.description: Hybridization, the exchange of genes between divergent lineages, is now recognized as widespread across eukaryotes and essential to understanding genome evolution. In this Review, Schumer and Rieseberg overview methodological advances facilitating recent progress, reassess the frequency, causes and consequences of hybridization, and highlight key open questions.

records.title: AI-based multimodal integration of genomics and electronic health records
records.description: This Review covers advances in artificial intelligence-based methods for multimodal modelling of genomics and electronic health record data, and the integration of these data into electronic-health-record-based research and clinical workflows to support genomics-enabled clinical decision, with an emphasis on governance and equitable implementation.

records.title: The genetics of complex gene expression phenotypes illuminated
records.description: Christian Landry reflects on a 2002 study by Brem, Yvert and colleagues, which combined yeast genetics and genome-wide expression profiling to reveal the genetic architecture underlying gene expression and transformed our understanding of regulatory variation.

records.title: Embracing non-linearity in human ageing
records.description: Ageing has often been conceptualized as a gradual, linear decline, yet growing evidence suggests it unfolds through dynamic, stage-specific transitions. In this Perspective, the authors examine such evidence across molecular and physiological systems and discuss analytical frameworks to identify non-linear transitions.

records.title: Towards quantifying immune diversity through HLA genomics
records.description: Computational metrics such as HLA evolutionary divergence offer new ways to quantify functional variation in antigen presentation. In this Comment, the authors discuss how population-scale genomics can benchmark these approaches and assess their potential as quantitative measures of human immune diversity.

records.title: Genomic, epigenomic and transcriptomic regulation of cellular senescence
records.description: Senescence — a complex, dynamic and heterogeneous stress-responsive cell state — shapes ageing biology and tissue homeostasis. This Review examines the molecular regulation of senescence initiation, maintenance and propagation, highlighting the need for revised mechanistic frameworks and biomarkers to define and target senescent cells.

records.title: Human genetics across levels of biological organization
records.description: Genetic variation influences biological processes across scales; however, deciphering how effects propagate from molecules to whole organisms remains a key challenge in human genetics. In this Review, Laman Trip and Beltrao discuss how to link genetic variation to mechanisms across interacting biological levels using network, single-cell and imaging approaches.

records.title: Stomata — guarding the gates against bacterial invasion
records.description: In this Journal Club, Tatsuya Nobori recalls a landmark paper by Melotto et al., who showed that stomata are active components of plant innate immunity rather than passive entry points for bacterial pathogens.

records.title: Folding a broken genome: the versatile roles of cohesin in genome maintenance
records.description: The protein complex cohesin shapes 3D genome organization through both cohesion and loop extrusion. The authors review the roles of these two mechanistic functions in the cellular response to DNA double-strand breaks, wherein cohesin acts to signal the presence of DNA damage, establish a repair environment, and catalyse the DNA repair process.

records.title: Genetic analysis of imaging-derived phenotypes
records.description: When integrated with genetic data, imaging-derived phenotypes (IDPs) enable large-scale analyses of genotype–phenotype relationships. Bian and Akey review analytical approaches to derive IDPs, key biological insights from genetic studies of imaging traits and emerging challenges in the rapidly evolving field of imaging genomics.

records.title: Building and applying pangenome references to capture genetic diversity
records.description: Pangenomes are genome references that integrate sequences from multiple individuals into graph-based or multi-haplotype representations, capturing genetic variation beyond a single linear reference. Here the authors review advances in assembling and applying human pangenome references, highlighting tools, insights and remaining challenges.

records.title: Genetic origins and constraints of evolutionary innovation
records.description: Evolutionary innovation emerges through the interplay of genetic novelty, genomic architecture and evolutionary constraint. Nature Reviews Genetics presents a Focus issue that explores the mechanisms that generate, integrate and shape biological diversity.

records.title: Single-cell four-omics with CHARM
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yujie Chen describes CHARM, a single-cell four-omics sequencing method that profiles genome conformation, chromatin accessibility, histone modifications and gene expression.

records.title: Molecular integration of seasonal temperature signals in flowering time control
records.description: Plants must accurately time flowering by integrating seasonal temperature cues to ensure reproductive success. This Review describes how two mechanisms — rapid transcriptional responses and long-term epigenetic memory — work together in parallel to robustly control flowering time, and it highlights that variation in these processes provides important information for the future of crops under a changing climate.

records.title: RBPscan measures protein–RNA interactions in living cells
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Dmitry Kretov and Daniel Cifuentes describe RBPscan (RNA-binding protein specificity and contextual analysis via nucleotide editing), a method that measures the strength of in vivo interactions between RNA binding proteins and their RNA targets.

records.title: Revisiting retinal and macular degeneration in the genomics era
records.description: Retinal and macular degeneration are major causes of vision loss around the globe. In this Review, Swaroop and Roska outline the genetic underpinnings of these eye diseases increasingly revealed by technological advances, while also highlighting mechanistic patterns that can inform therapeutic intervention to restore vision.

records.title: How evolution builds three morphs from one genome
records.description: Sarah Kocher reflects on two influential 2016 studies in the ruff that demonstrated how a large genomic inversion links variation across multiple traits into a single ‘supergene’.

records.title: Advancing the applications of liquid biopsies in oncology
records.description: In this Review, Valpione et al. discuss how the current applications of liquid biopsies in precision oncology might be expanded to provide a more holistic and personalized view of cancer and to improve cancer diagnosis and treatment.

records.title: Pleiotropic effects of cis -regulatory mutations
records.description: In this Comment, Patricia Wittkopp revisits assumptions that cis -regulatory mutations are weakly pleiotropic, ultimately calling for more data to assess the extent to which they are less pleiotropic and deleterious than trans -regulatory mutations.

records.title: Transposable elements as catalysts of evolutionary innovation
records.description: In this Comment, Cedric Feschotte highlights evidence from diverse lineages showing that transposable elements are key drivers of evolutionary innovation, repeatedly introducing regulatory and coding sequences that reconfigure genome function.

records.title: Adaptation: by giant leaps or many tiny steps?
records.description: In this Comment, the authors argue that understanding the genetic basis of adaptation requires considering the genetic architecture and ecological properties of traits under selection. They propose a framework that predicts when evolution proceeds by many small changes or few large-effect variants, and when its genetic basis should be predictable across populations and species.

records.title: Written in blood: DNA methylation in liquid biopsy
records.description: In this Journal Club, Chatterjee and Rodger highlight two studies by Guo et al. and Shen et al. that demonstrated how genome-wide DNA methylation profiling enables sensitive detection and classification of tumour-derived cell-free DNA, advancing epigenetic approaches in liquid biopsy for cancer diagnostics.

records.title: Single-cell trimodal profiling with scHiCAR
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yueyuan Xu and Xiaolin Wei discuss scHiCAR (single-cell Hi-C with assay for transposase-accessible chromatin and RNA sequencing), a trimodal single-cell method for simultaneously profiling gene expression, chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organization.

records.title: Translating functional molecular knowledge into crop-breeding success
records.description: In this Perspective, Ramstein and colleagues discuss the use of emerging machine learning tools for function-informed prioritization of variants for plant breeding; they outline future applications in which precision breeding strategies have the potential to be most effective.

records.title: The discovery of gene imprinting
records.description: In this Journal Club, Mary Gehring recalls a 1970 paper from Jerry Kermicle, which used elegant maize genetics to show that alleles behave differently depending on parental origin, laying the conceptual foundation for gene imprinting.

records.title: The long reach of the Red Queen
records.description: Red Queen dynamics describe a mode of evolution in which interacting biological entities continually adapt and counteradapt. This Comment discusses the pervasiveness of these dynamics within genomes, which can involve selfish genetic elements, and highlights building evidence that they can even drive compensatory coevolution among subunits of essential protein complexes.

records.title: Computational approaches for multimodal lineage tracing
records.description: Multimodal lineage tracing links heritable ancestry with single-cell molecular states to reveal how cell fates emerge during development, regeneration and disease. In this Review, the authors survey key computational challenges and methods for phylogenetic inference, fate mapping and gene programme discovery.

records.title: Time matters: circadian genetics and the molecular logic of human health and disease
records.description: The circadian clock controls transcriptional and signalling networks across tissues to maintain homeostasis, with pathological consequences to its disruption. Kuo et al. review our understanding of circadian genetic and molecular mechanisms in health and disease, as well as emerging opportunities to probe and therapeutically target circadian regulation.

records.title: Immune-evasive DNA integration with INSTALL
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Connor Tou presents INSTALL, a recombinase-driven, kilobase-scale DNA integration method that employs partially duplexed circular single-stranded DNA to evade the cellular immune system.

records.title: The unbearable presence of senescent cells in ageing
records.description: Chanhee Kang highlights two papers by Baker et al. and Acosta et al. that established a role for senescent cells in age-related pathologies and revealed how the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) can influence neighbouring cells.

records.title: Resolving structural variants in pangenome graphs with Swave
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Songbo Wang introduces Swave, an AI-enhanced sequence-to-image method capable of detecting complex SVs from pangenome graphs.

records.title: Evolutionary genetics of ageing
records.description: Modern humans increasingly live long enough to experience late-life consequences of genetic and molecular systems shaped by natural selection. In this Review, the authors integrate evolutionary genetics and genetic evidence to explain why ageing evolves, why longevity varies across species and individuals, and how these insights inform healthspan extension.

records.title: RNA design across eras: from covariance models to modern generative AI
records.description: In this Journal Club, Annalisa Marsico describes a 1994 paper by Eddy and Durbin that formalized RNA sequence analysis with covariance models, which are powerful tools more recently applied to generative machine learning models for RNA design.

records.title: Prime editing: redefining precision genome editing
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Qiupeng Lin recalls the 2019 paper by Anzalone et al. that introduced prime editing, and reflects on the impact of this technology on genome biology and beyond.

records.title: Nutrition signals the brain to reactivate quiescent neural stem cells
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Hongyan Wang highlights two papers that elucidated the signalling mechanisms and inter-organ communication involved in neural stem cell reactivation in Drosophila melanogaster .

records.title: Mechanisms of DNA specificity in chromatin remodelling
records.description: In this Journal Club, Lu Bai highlights a 2021 paper by Donovan et al. that brought mechanistic clarity to the question of how chromatin remodellers achieve DNA specificity, which had been difficult to address beyond correlated localization patterns between chromatin remodellers and transcription factors.

records.title: The epigenetic nature of X chromosome inactivation
records.description: In this Journal Club, Claudia Keller Valsecchi recalls two seminal studies by Csankovszki et al. and by Wutz and Jaenisch that defined X-chromosome inactivation as an epigenetic process by revealing when Xist is required and when silencing becomes Xist -independent.

records.title: When the genome learned its own vocabulary
records.description: In this Journal Club article, Maria Brbić discusses DeepSEA, a pioneering deep convolutional neural network to predict functional effects of non-coding variants, and its influence on computational genomics.

records.title: Reading cell division histories from the methylome
records.description: In this Journal Club, Shou-Wen Wang recalls a seminal paper by Yatabe et al., which harnessed stochastic DNA methylation patterns in the human colon for epigenetic lineage tracing, and influenced the development of the computational framework MethylTree two decades later.

records.title: TimeVault: a synthetic time capsule for transcriptome storage
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yu-Kai Chao describes TimeVault, an inducible system that can store transcriptomes at defined time points, enabling temporal changes in transcriptional state to be linked to biological events.

records.title: More than meets the eye(spot): evolution through co-option of developmental programmes
records.description: In this Journal Club, Francisca Real recalls a 1999 paper by Keys et al. that dissected the mechanistic underpinnings of butterfly wing spot development, which ultimately provided one of the earliest and clearest examples of phenotypic evolution by genetic co-option.

records.title: Tools and tactics for studying alternative splicing
records.description: In this Review, Sousa-Luís and Carmo-Fonseca discuss the various tools available to detect and quantify alternative splicing, functionally test splice isoforms and investigate the link between genetic variation, splicing and disease.

records.title: CRISPR–Cas-based live cell imaging of genome dynamics
records.description: In this Review, Zhu et al. outline the various CRISPR-based tools recently built for dynamic DNA and RNA imaging, which have provided insights into various molecular mechanisms. The authors also discuss the important parameters to consider when using these tools, and how to approach the quantitative image analysis.

records.title: DNA assembly with Sidewinder via 3-way junctions
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Kaihang Wang describes Sidewinder, a new tool that leverages ‘page number’ barcodes and 3-way junctions to scarlessly assemble DNA with high fidelity, expanding the scope of what DNA writing can achieve.

records.title: Unlocking the potential of pedigree genomics via precision governance
records.description: China’s large, multi-generational pedigrees provide a distinctive genomic resource for precision medicine but present a governance challenge. We propose a new framework that addresses the core contradiction between individual-centric governance and the collective nature of these genomic datasets.

records.title: Unlocking the potential of pedigree genomics via precision governance
records.description: China’s large, multi-generational pedigrees provide a distinctive genomic resource for precision medicine but present a governance challenge. We propose a new framework that addresses the core contradiction between individual-centric governance and the collective nature of these genomic datasets.

records.title: How classical genetics uncovered key determinants of TE silencing
records.description: In this Journal Club, Emilie Brasset highlights a 1995 publication by Prud’homme et al., who designed a clever genetic assay to identify a gene important for TE silencing, which provided a crucial foundation for later studies to unravel the underlying mechanisms.

records.title: Genetic influences on haematopoiesis
records.description: Haematopoiesis is a classic process for understanding the genetic basis of human health and disease. In this Review, Poeschla and Sankaran discuss this history and more recent advances in our understanding of the roles of rare variants in monogenic blood diseases, germline and somatic variants in population-level variation, as well as emerging therapeutic applications.

records.title: Author Correction: Forensic genetics in the omics era
Recoding genomes with programmed ribosomal frameshifting
records.description: In this Journal Club, Yousuf A. Khan recounts a landmark study published in 1985 by Jacks and Varmus that documented programmed ribosomal frameshifting in retroviruses, which later inspired Yousuf to search for this phenomenon in vertebrates.

records.title: Next-generation programmable cell therapies for precision medicine
records.description: In this Review, Teixeira et al. discuss emerging strategies for developing and improving engineered-cell therapies. They outline progress from ex vivo engineered autologous cells to in vivo reprogramming, advances in delivery systems and the remaining translational barriers.

records.title: Gene regulatory networks: from correlative models to causal explanations
records.description: In this Perspective, Maizels and Briscoe discuss the limitations of current models of gene regulatory networks and outline solutions to harness data abundance without compromising explanatory power.

records.title: Epistasis and co-adaptation in bacterial genome evolution
records.description: Bacterial genome evolution is shaped by epistasis, which can constrain or promote specific evolutionary paths. The authors review how integrating the effects of epistatic interactions into population-scale analyses can improve genotype–phenotype mapping and provide a deeper understanding of the complex traits that shape the microbial world.

records.title: Charting single-cell lineages with synthetic and natural barcodes
records.description: In this Review, Rodriguez-Fraticelli and Parreno discuss advances in single-cell lineage-tracing methods and how their application to diverse biological processes, such as development, ageing and cancer, is challenging prevailing views and providing new insights.

records.title: From DNA microarrays to somatic mosaicism in population cohorts
records.description: Chikashi Terao recalls a paper by Loh et al., which introduced a highly sensitive algorithm to detect low-fraction chromosomal mosaicism from SNP array data, enabling large-scale mapping of clonal haematopoiesis.

records.title: A codon-resolved view of subcellular translation with LOCL-TL
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Jingchuan Luo discusses LOCL-TL (LOV domain-controlled ligase for translation localization), a method they helped develop to enable the study of subcellular translation at codon-level resolution.

records.title: Annotating genomes at increased scale and resolution
records.description: In this Review, Ji et al. overview how rapidly advancing experimental and computational methods are enabling improved and automated annotation of gene structure and function, providing researchers with genome annotation resources of unprecedented scale and resolution.

records.title: Bridging technical innovation and computational advances in studies of RNA–protein assemblies
